**Hamilton** continues to dominate the conversation, earning the highest critic score at 90/100. Lin-Manuel Miranda's hip-hop historical epic remains as groundbreaking as ever, proving that its revolutionary approach to musical theater hasn't lost momentum even years after its debut.

Among newer arrivals, **Maybe Happy Ending** stands out with an 85/100 score, captivating critics with its unexpectedly moving robot love story that brings genuine originality to the Broadway musical format. Meanwhile, **Oh, Mary!** has emerged as the season's comedic sensation, with Cole Escola's absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed narcissist earning enthusiastic raves for its audacious humor.

The roster balances fresh voices with enduring classics. Long-running spectacles like **The Lion King** and **The Book of Mormon** maintain their strong critical standing, while **Ragtime**'s timely revival demonstrates how classic musicals can resonate with contemporary audiences. From the folk-opera innovation of **Hadestown** to the stripped-down vitality of **Chicago**, this month's selections showcase the remarkable range of storytelling approaches thriving on Broadway stages.

Whether you're drawn to groundbreaking new works or reimagined classics, March 2026 offers theatergoers an exceptional array of critically acclaimed productions to explore.

best-broadway-plays.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves deeper into 2026, the play landscape offers an eclectic mix of intimate character studies and spectacular technical showcases. This month's selections range from absurdist comedy to wizarding world magic, with an average critic score of 79/100 across four productions.

Leading the pack is **Oh, Mary!**, Cole Escola's irreverent reimagining of Mary Todd Lincoln as a cabaret-obsessed inebriate. With 84/100 from 32 reviews, this absurdist farce continues to draw enthusiastic critical reception for its audacious comedic vision and willingness to skewer historical reverence in favor of riotous entertainment.

**Every Brilliant Thing** brings Daniel Radcliffe to Broadway in an intimate, interactive exploration of depression and finding reasons to live. Though working with a smaller sample of just 2 reviews at 83/100, the production demonstrates the enduring appeal of stripped-down theatrical storytelling, even as critics note some reservations about its earnestness.

On the spectacle-driven end of the spectrum, **Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** maintains its position as a technical marvel, earning praise across 69 reviews for its stagecraft and magical illusions, despite mixed reactions to its narrative choices. Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** delivers the visual pyrotechnics Netflix fans expect, though its three-hour runtime and storytelling struggles have tempered critical enthusiasm.

The current slate reflects Broadway's broad church: productions succeeding on sharp writing and performance (Oh, Mary!), others on sheer technical ambition (Cursed Child, Stranger Things), and some betting on star power and emotional resonance (Every Brilliant Thing). Whether you're drawn to intimate storytelling or large-scale spectacle, this month's offerings provide multiple entry points into what Broadway plays can achieve.

best-broadway-shows-for-kids.intro:

The production remains a masterclass in how visual artistry can elevate familiar material into something transcendent.

**Harry Potter and the Cursed Child** follows closely with an 82/100 from 69 reviews, offering a more divisive experience. While critics universally acclaim its spectacular stagecraft and magical illusions, they note the narrative doesn't always match the technical wizardry on display. The show nonetheless delivers the kind of theatrical magic that younger audiences particularly respond to.

The remaining selections—**Aladdin**, **& Juliet**, **Wicked**, and **MJ The Musical**—each score between 69 and 71/100, representing solid if less groundbreaking options. These productions tend to prioritize spectacle and recognizable music over narrative innovation, with critics noting their crowd-pleasing qualities while acknowledging formulaic elements.

What emerges from the critical consensus is that Broadway's current family offerings favor visual spectacle and technical achievement, sometimes at the expense of storytelling depth. Parents should consider whether their children will be more engaged by puppetry and stagecraft (The Lion King), magical illusions (Harry Potter), or high-energy musical numbers (the remaining shows). Review the full details below to find the best match for your family's interests and your child's age.

The month's highest-rated show, **Ragtime**, arrives as both a timely and timeless choice. This revival of the sweeping American epic earns widespread critical acclaim, with particular praise directed toward Joshua Henry's commanding performance and the score's enduring emotional impact. After 30 reviews, the production stands as March's most consistently praised offering.

On a more intimate scale, **Every Brilliant Thing** brings Daniel Radcliffe to Broadway in an interactive one-person play exploring depression and the small joys that sustain us. Despite matching Ragtime's 83/100 score, the production has garnered only 2 reviews so far, with critics acknowledging its earnest intentions while finding the execution somewhat underwhelming—though Radcliffe's star power continues to draw attention.

Meanwhile, **Two Strangers (Carry a Cake Across New York)** charms critics as a modest British import, offering a sincere two-hander that trades spectacle for heartfelt simplicity. The romantic comedy scores 78/100, winning audiences with its unpretentious approach.

**Chess** rounds out the month as its most polarizing entry. While the ABBA score and vocal performances from Lea Michele, Aaron Tveit, and the ensemble dazzle, critics remain divided on the production's overall success, resulting in a 65/100 average.

Whether you're drawn to sweeping historical drama, intimate character studies, or old-fashioned musical spectacle, March's Broadway lineup offers multiple entry points for theatergoers seeking their next show.

best-broadway-shows-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of a season dramatically cut short. While the pandemic would soon darken theaters for over a year, the productions that managed to premiere in those early months have left a lasting impression on critics and audiences alike.

Leading our selection is **Les Misérables**, which scores highest with its grittier reboot at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre. This reimagined production strips away some of the original's spectacle in favor of a rawer, more intimate approach that has won over most critics, even as it leaves traditionalists skeptical.

**A Soldier's Play** stands out as perhaps the season's most culturally significant production—Charles Fuller's Pulitzer Prize-winning drama finally receiving its long-overdue Broadway premiere. The stellar revival demonstrates how the play's examination of race, power, and identity within the military remains devastatingly relevant, earning widespread critical acclaim.

Other notable entries include **Grand Horizons**, a boulevard comedy elevated by the legendary performances of Jane Alexander and James Cromwell as a divorcing elderly couple, and **My Name is Lucy Barton**, which showcases Laura Linney's luminous solo performance in this adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel, even if critics remain divided on the theatrical adaptation itself.

The five shows featured here average a solid 75/100 critical score, reflecting a season of ambitious work that ranged from radical reinterpretations of classics to important dramatic revivals. For theatergoers interested in exploring what made early 2020 significant for Broadway, these productions offer essential viewing that captures both the artistic ambitions and cultural conversations of that pivotal moment.

best-broadway-shows-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Shows from 2021

As we reach March 2026, the Broadway shows that opened in 2021 continue to represent a pivotal moment in theater history—marking not just the industry's post-pandemic reopening, but also a period of remarkable artistic innovation and risk-taking.

The ten productions featured here maintain an impressive average critic score of 81/100, reflecting the exceptional quality of work that emerged during Broadway's return. Leading the group is **Dana H.**, Lucas Hnath's unconventional docudrama featuring Deirdre O'Connell's stunning lip-sync performance, which critics continue to describe as mesmerizing and unforgettable. Close behind, **The Phantom of the Opera**—Andrew Lloyd Webber's enduring mega-musical—proves that spectacle and infectious melodies can transcend critical debates about camp and coolness.

The 2021 season notably embraced intimate, experimental work alongside traditional blockbusters. **Pass Over**, Antoinette Chinonye Nwandu's urgent drama blending Beckett and Exodus, served as Broadway's official reopening production—a powerful statement about the theater's priorities. Meanwhile, **The Lehman Trilogy** delivered epic scope through minimalist means, earning widespread acclaim for its theatrical ambition.

This collection also showcases transformative revivals, including Marianne Elliott's gender-swapped **Company** and Rebecca Frecknall's immersive **Cabaret at the Kit Kat Club**, both demonstrating how fresh perspectives can illuminate classic material. Verbatim theater found its place too, with **Is This a Room** proving that FBI transcripts could become pulse-pounding drama.

Whether you're drawn to experimental docudrama, reimagined classics, or new American plays, these productions represent the breadth and vitality of Broadway's 2021 renaissance. Explore the full list to discover which shows align with your theatrical tastes.

Jackson's meta-musical about a Black queer writer, brings bold originality to Broadway, while Suzan-Lori Parks' **Topdog/Underdog** revival crackles with renewed energy decades after its premiere. The season balances intimate character studies like **Mike Birbiglia: The Old Man & The Pool** with provocative satires such as **Ain't No Mo'**, demonstrating the breadth of theatrical storytelling.

With an average critical score of 83/100, these productions represent some of the finest theater of the decade. Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting favorites, this collection offers an essential guide to 2022's most accomplished Broadway productions.

best-broadway-plays-2020.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays from 2020

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that opened in 2020 represent a fascinating snapshot of theater interrupted and transformed. That year's abbreviated season, cut short by the pandemic shutdown, produced a diverse slate of productions ranging from bold reimaginings of classics to intimate character studies.

Leading our selection is a grittier reboot of **Les Misérables** at the refurbished Sondheim Theatre, earning an 83/100 from critics who largely embrace its fresh approach to the beloved musical, though some traditionalists remain unconvinced. Close behind, **A Soldier's Play** makes its long-overdue Broadway debut with a stellar revival of Charles Fuller's Pulitzer-winning drama, proving that its examination of race, power, and justice within a 1940s military base remains devastatingly relevant—critics award it a 78/100.

The season also features **Grand Horizons**, a boulevard comedy about a divorcing elderly couple that critics find pleasant if familiar, elevated considerably by performances from Jane Alexander and James Cromwell. Laura Linney commands the stage solo in **My Name is Lucy Barton**, an adaptation of Elizabeth Strout's novel that divides critics despite universal praise for Linney's luminous work. Rounding out the selection, Ivo van Hove's radical **West Side Story** reimagining proves deeply polarizing, with its striking video design and visceral staging earning both passionate advocates and fierce detractors.

With an average critic score of 75/100 across these five productions, the 2020 season demonstrates Broadway's ongoing tension between honoring theatrical tradition and pushing toward bold reinvention. Explore the full reviews and details below to find which production speaks to your theatrical sensibilities.

best-broadway-plays-2021.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2021

As we look back from March 2026, the Broadway plays that debuted in 2021 represent a remarkable chapter in theater history—the season when live performance roared back to life after the pandemic shutdown. These productions arrived with urgency, innovation, and artistic ambition, and five years later, they continue to define what contemporary theater can achieve.

The standout among this class is **Dana H.**, an unconventional docudrama that earns the highest critical score (86/100) through Deirdre O'Connell's mesmerizing lip-sync performance to a real interview with playwright Lucas Hnath's mother. Critics describe it as unforgettable and groundbreaking in its approach to theatrical storytelling. Meanwhile, **The Phantom of the Opera**, though representing Broadway's commercial past rather than its experimental future, proves that Lloyd Webber's mega-musical spectacle still captivates audiences and critics alike with its infectious melodies and grand staging.

The 2021 season also brought crucial voices to Broadway's stages. **Pass Over** earned its place as the first play to reopen Broadway after the shutdown, blending Beckett and Exodus into an urgent examination of Black American experience. **The Lehman Trilogy** delivered epic scope with intimate performances, while experimental works like **Is This a Room** transformed FBI transcripts into pulse-pounding drama.

With an impressive average critical score of 81/100 across these ten productions, the 2021 plays demonstrate exceptional quality and range—from Ruben Santiago-Hudson's virtuosic solo turn in **Lackawanna Blues** to the gender-swapped reimagining of Sondheim's **Company**. Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies or immersive theatrical spectacles, this guide helps you discover which of these acclaimed productions deserves your attention.

best-broadway-plays-2022.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2022

As we look back from March 2026, the 2022 Broadway season stands out as a remarkable year that brought both innovative new voices and essential revivals to the stage. Four years later, many of these productions continue to resonate with audiences and critics alike, proving their staying power in the theatrical canon.

The season's highest-rated show, **Kimberly Akimbo**, exemplifies the year's creative achievement. This quirky musical about a teenage girl with a rare aging condition balances comedy and heartbreak with near-perfect precision, earning an impressive 88/100 from critics. Close behind, **Into the Woods** offered audiences a stripped-down Sondheim revival that served as both a fitting tribute to the late composer and a fresh interpretation of his classic work.

What distinguishes 2022's theatrical landscape is its concentration of Pulitzer Prize-winning material. **A Strange Loop**, **Topdog/Underdog**, **Leopoldstadt**, **Between Riverside and Crazy**, **How I Learned to Drive**, and **Cost of Living** all brought Pulitzer-recognized writing to Broadway stages, creating an unusually literary season. These productions tackled weighty subjects—from racial identity and family trauma to caregiving and sexual abuse—with unflinching honesty and artistic ambition.

The year also showcased theatrical diversity in form, from Tom Stoppard's sweeping historical drama **Leopoldstadt** to Mike Birbiglia's intimate solo show **The Old Man & The Pool**, and Jordan E. Cooper's provocative sketch-comedy satire **Ain't No Mo'**. With an average critic score of 83/100 across these ten productions, the 2022 season delivered consistently strong work that challenged, moved, and entertained in equal measure.

Whether you're discovering these shows for the first time or revisiting familiar favorites, this collection represents some of Broadway's most critically acclaimed work from a standout year.

best-broadway-plays-2023.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays That Opened in 2023

As we look back from March 2026, the plays that debuted in 2023 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and artistic achievement. That season proved to be a watershed moment for Broadway drama, delivering everything from long-overdue revivals to boundary-pushing new works that still resonate with contemporary audiences.

Leading the field is Maria Friedman's acclaimed revival of **Merrily We Roll Along**, which triumphantly rehabilitates Stephen Sondheim's notorious 1981 flop with emotionally resonant performances that finally unlock the show's potential. The production stands alongside **Appropriate**, Branden Jacobs-Jenkins's searing family drama that critics hail as a modern masterpiece, powered by Sarah Paulson's blistering performance. Meanwhile, **Stranger Things: The First Shadow** proves that theatrical adaptations of popular IP can transcend mere fan service, earning praise for its technically stunning stagecraft and compelling storytelling.

The 2023 season also championed vital revivals that speak to ongoing cultural conversations. **Purlie Victorious** brings Ossie Davis's 1961 satire back to Broadway with bracingly relevant humor, while **Parade** finds urgent contemporary resonance in its historical subject matter. Solo performances shine through Alex Edelman's **Just for Us** and Jodie Comer's tour de force in **Prima Facie**, demonstrating the enduring power of one-person storytelling.

With an impressive average critic score of 82/100 across these ten productions, the plays of 2023 represent a high-water mark for dramatic excellence on Broadway. Whether you're drawn to intimate character studies, ambitious revivals, or innovative new voices, this collection offers a comprehensive guide to the season's most critically acclaimed theatrical experiences.

best-broadway-plays-2024.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays Opening in March 2026

As Broadway moves through March 2026, the shows that debuted in 2024 continue to demonstrate remarkable staying power and critical acclaim. This collection of ten productions—averaging an impressive 84/100 critical score—represents some of the most innovative and celebrated theater of recent years.

Leading the field is **Stereophonic**, David Adjmi's meticulously crafted drama about a 1970s rock band in the studio. With 22 reviews scoring it at 88/100, critics consistently describe it as a theatrical marvel that authentically captures the messy, electric creative process. Close behind, **Operation Mincemeat** (86/100) proves that grassroots British musicals can triumph on Broadway, earning praise for its inventive energy and ensemble work that justified its journey from fringe success to the West End and beyond.

The diversity of this year's standouts is striking. **CATS: The Jellicle Ball** reimagines Andrew Lloyd Webber's classic through the lens of ballroom culture, while **Maybe Happy Ending** offers one of Broadway's most original concepts in years: a tender robot love story that critics find surprisingly emotional. Cole Escola's **Oh, Mary!** provides riotous comedy with its absurdist take on Mary Todd Lincoln, and Audra McDonald brings fresh interpretation to the iconic Mama Rose in **Gypsy**.

From intimate dramas like **Mary Jane** to lavish revivals like **Oliver!** and innovative hybrids like **Illinoise**, these productions showcase Broadway's range and creative ambition. Whether you're drawn to rock-era authenticity, ballroom spectacle, or quietly devastating family drama, this season's critically acclaimed offerings provide multiple entry points into exceptional theater.

best-broadway-plays-2025.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays: March 2026

As Broadway moves through the spring of 2026, the 2025 season continues to resonate with audiences, offering an impressive range of theatrical experiences from intimate dramas to spectacular family entertainment. This month's guide showcases ten productions that opened last year and maintain strong critical standing, with an average score of 84/100.

Ivo van Hove's minimalist revival of **All My Sons** leads the field, earning widespread acclaim for its emotional intensity and exceptional ensemble work. The production demonstrates how a stripped-down aesthetic can amplify Arthur Miller's devastating family drama. Close behind, the 20th-anniversary revival of **The 25th Annual Putnam County Spelling Bee** proves the musical's enduring charm, with critics celebrating its airtight writing and emotional resonance.

The season's diversity is evident in offerings like **Paddington The Musical**, where a remarkably lifelike bear puppet captivates both families and critics, and **Liberation**, Bess Wohl's ambitious feminist memory play that tackles timely themes through superbly acted ensemble work. Musical theater enthusiasts can also experience the emotional power of **Ragtime**'s revival, featuring Joshua Henry's powerhouse performance, or the intoxicating music of **Buena Vista Social Club**.

Sanaz Toossi's Pulitzer-winning **English** brings intellectual rigor to its exploration of language and identity, while Branden Jacobs-Jenkins' **Purpose** delivers another characteristically sharp family drama. Rounding out the list are the darkly comic **Dead Outlaw** and the experimental **The Infinite Wrench**.

Whether you're drawn to classic American drama, innovative musicals, or contemporary playwriting, this selection offers compelling options for theatergoers this March.

best-broadway-plays-2026.intro:
# Best Broadway Plays of 2026

March 2026 brings a modest start to the year for new Broadway plays, with only one production making its debut so far. While the season is just beginning to take shape, early offerings reveal the enduring appeal of intimate storytelling and star power on the Great White Way.

**Every Brilliant Thing** leads as the sole new play opening this year to date, earning an 83/100 from critics. The interactive production tackles weighty themes of depression and gratitude through audience participation, with Daniel Radcliffe's marquee name drawing significant attention. While reviewers appreciate the play's earnest approach to mental health and its engaging format, the critical consensus suggests the execution doesn't fully realize the material's potential. Nevertheless, the combination of Radcliffe's star appeal and the show's participatory nature makes it a notable entry in this year's theatrical landscape.

With an average score of 83/100 across the year's debuts, the quality bar sits at a respectable level, though the limited sample size means the season's trajectory remains wide open. The spring and fall traditionally bring Broadway's most ambitious offerings, so theatergoers can anticipate a more robust slate of new plays in the months ahead.

As March unfolds and producers announce their upcoming productions, audiences should keep an eye on schedules for additional openings that will fill out the 2026 theatrical calendar. Whether you're drawn to celebrity-led productions like **Every Brilliant Thing** or waiting to see what else emerges, check back regularly as more plays debut throughout the year.
